messages.author: 4525396ad5bfc811
messages.subject: Hierarchical phylogenetic regression problems
parts:
Hi stan users,

I am having a lot of trouble with a multi-level model that I am helping a colleague with. I am trying to model individuals of several tree species' responses to nitrogen and phosphorous and then model the species responses to nitrogen as a function of several plant traits. The model is essentially a direct copy of the  multivariate regression example from the stan manual (pp 64-69). The only difference is that at the second level, the multivariate normal VCV matrix is being multiplied by a phylogenetic correlation matrix. This correlation matrix has a lambda parameter multiplied to the off-diagonals to estimate the "strength" of phylogenetic history's effects on the regression (between 0 & 1). The model works well enough when the higher level just  contains an intercept term, but once I add another level of predictor variables, mixing becomes horrible and I get lots of divergence warnings. I am worried I messed up the math but haven't been able to figure out what's wrong. Any advice would be greatly appreciated! Ultimately I would like to estimate the trait means for each species from the data (which have missing values), but at the moment I can't even get the model to work when the trait means are fixed as data.

The model and data are included as attachments. My session info is listed below. 

Thanks so much for any help!

Best,

Zach Marion

Sorry nobody's answered. I'm not good enough at linear
algebra to help out. You'll find the harder the problem, the
less likely you are to get a response on this or any other list.

The best I can suggest is that you try to write the
functionality out as cleanly as possible and test by
printing before and after in simple test cases where
you know the answer.

- Bob
